name: autoaway
author: Gerardo Canosa
description: Away when you're idle or nobody is attached, back when you return; on or off per network, away and back announced per channel if you like

name: awaylog
author: Gerardo Canosa
description: Your highlights and private messages while you were away or detached, summed up in each network's console when you come back

name: preview
author: Gerardo Canosa
description: A preview under links people post: in the webchat the page's title, description and picture, the picture itself for image links and a player for audio and video links; in the terminal the title and description as text

name: seen
author: Gerardo Canosa
description: /seen nick: when and where someone was last seen talking, joining, leaving, quitting or renaming; answers !seen in channels you pick

name: proxy
author: Gerardo Canosa
description: Connects the networks you pick through a SOCKS4/SOCKS5 or HTTP proxy, or an SSH jump host; the others stay direct

name: push
author: Gerardo Canosa
description: Your highlights and private messages pushed to your phone, tablet or browser while you're away or nothing is attached: ntfy (no account) or a Telegram bot; /push test

name: keepnick
author: Gerardo Canosa
description: Takes your nick back once it's free: when its holder leaves, or by asking the server every 30 seconds

name: remind
author: Gerardo Canosa
description: /remind 10m text, /remind 18:30 text: a reminder in that tab, saved across restarts; /remind lists them

name: pmguard
author: Gerardo Canosa
description: Private messages from people you haven't let through are held, not opened, and get a notice saying so; /pmguard allow nick, or Allow PMs in the nicklist's right click, opens the query with what they said; the allowed list, per network, is in /plugin's window

name: pasteguard
author: Gerardo Canosa
description: A paste of several lines into a channel or query becomes a pastebin link (paste.rs by default), so you don't flood

name: screensaver
author: Gerardo Canosa
description: A screensaver for the terminal and the webchat after some idle minutes: digital rain, floating particles or a quiet sky of drifting stars; with lock on, waking asks for the lock password; locking iSekur starts one behind the password box

name: autosort
author: Gerardo Canosa
description: Keeps the tabs grouped by network, each network's status tab first, then its channels and queries by name

name: tts
author: Gerardo Canosa
description: Reads messages aloud: with this machine's speech engine (say on macOS; speech-dispatcher, espeak-ng, flite or festival on Linux and BSD), in the webchat's browser voice, or both; /tts engines shows which engines this system has

name: lolcat
author: Gerardo Canosa
description: The messages in the channels you pick, in rainbow, fire, ice, forest, neon, sunset, pastel or your theme's own nick colors, on your screens only: nothing is sent in color, the logs stay plain

name: nickcolors
author: Gerardo Canosa
description: Nicks in the colors the chat gives them: the nicks said inside a message and/or the user list, each in its own color (and you in yours), on your screens only: nothing is sent in color, the logs stay plain

name: zen
author: Gerardo Canosa
description: /zen: only the chat, in a column in the middle, the last lines bright and the ones before them dimmed, in the mono theme; the tabs, nicklist, topic and status bar hide. In the terminal, the webchat or both. /zen again or Esc brings everything back

name: radio
author: Gerardo Canosa
description: /radio: 24/7 radio, audio only. YouTube's live channels (Claude FM, State FM, Pink Floyd style, 80s and synthwave radios) and plain internet radio (SomaFM, Radio Paradise); a window with a cassette, a filter, a favorite star and mute. The webchat plays it, on a phone too with the screen locked; the terminal plays it in the background. Needs ffmpeg (and yt-dlp for YouTube) on the machine iSekur runs on

name: eventshidemgr
author: Gerardo Canosa
description: Folds runs of joins, parts, quits, nick changes and, if you switch them on, hostname changes, mode changes, kicks and topic changes into one row, "3 joined, 2 left, 1 mode set", in the terminal and the webchat. A click opens the run and folds it again, and so does leaving the tab. Your own events and every message end a run. A setting for each kind (joins, leaves, nicks, hosts, modes, kicks, topics), the nicks in the row (names), and the summary rows kept in a /quiet tab (quiet = fold). On your screens only

name: twilight
author: Gerardo Canosa
description: Warms the colors after dark, like f.lux or Night Shift, in the terminal and the webchat and whatever the theme. Night is sunset to sunrise where you are (a city or coordinates, so iSekur on a server in another country still follows your sun) or hours you pick. It changes over minutes, switching it on or off takes a minute too, and a preview sweeps day to night and back. A window with a sun and a moon, /twilight preview, a manual temperature, a red-only darkroom

name: dropzone
author: Gerardo Canosa
description: Give iSekur a file and it goes to a file host, and a box asks what to do with the link: send it to the tab, copy it, or send it to another channel. Drag a file onto the webchat (the page shows what letting go does), paste a screenshot, tap the paperclip on a phone, drop a file on the terminal or /upload it
